---

### Translation *(derivative — the original governs)*

> On 5 March 1698 (1698-03-05), was baptized Pieter, son of Jan Hendricksz and Maria Willems. Witnesses were Cornelis de Vries and Aaltje Jans.

---

### Key Terms & Annotations

| Original | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| *gedoopt* | baptized | Event recorded is **baptism**, not birth; birth date not given |
| *soon* | son | Archaic spelling of *zoon*; standard 17th-c. Dutch orthography |
| *Hendricksz* | son of Hendrick | Patronymic suffix *-sz* = abbreviated *-szoon* ("Hendrick's son") — Jan's father was named Hendrick |
| *Willems* | (daughter) of Willem | Patronymic surname; Maria's father was named Willem |
| *Getuigen* | witnesses | Dutch Reformed usage — **not** Catholic godparents; these are witnesses to the baptism ceremony, theologically distinct |
| *Aaltje* | feminine given name | Dutch diminutive, often a form of *Adelheid*; common in the Netherlands |
| *Jans* | (daughter) of Jan | Patronymic surname on Aaltje — her father was named Jan |

---

### What Matters Genealogically

- **Pieter** — male child; the date 1698-03-05 is his **baptism** date only. Dutch Reformed registers typically do not record the birth date; a separate search for a birth entry may be needed, or the birth date may be inferred as a few days prior.

- **Aaltje Jans** — witness; her patronymic (*Jans* = daughter of Jan) raises the question of whether she is related to Jan Hendricksz or to the family more broadly — a FAN cluster worth investigating.

| Original term | Meaning & notes |

---

### Original Text (as provided)

> En la Ciudad de México, a quince de enero de mil setecientos cincuenta, yo, el infrascrito cura, bauticé solemnemente a Josefa María, española, hija legítima de Don Juan de Aguilar y de Doña María Ramírez. *(Text provided as a typed transcription — no paleographic reading required.)*

---

### Translation *(derivative — the original governs)*

> In the City of Mexico, on the fifteenth of January of seventeen hundred and fifty (1750-01-15), I, the undersigned parish priest, solemnly baptized Josefa María, a Spaniard [of Spanish caste], legitimate daughter of Don Juan de Aguilar and Doña María Ramírez. Her godparents were Don Pedro Gómez and Doña Ana López, to whom I advised [them of] their obligation and spiritual kinship.

---

### Key Term Annotations

| Original Term | Translation | Genealogical Significance |
|---|---|---|
| *infrascrito cura* | undersigned parish priest | Identifies the officiant role; the priest's full name would typically appear in a signed rubric at the end of the page — check the full folio |
| *bauticé solemnemente* | I solemnly baptized | **Solemn** baptism (*bautismo solemne*) = the full ceremonial rite. Distinguishes it from an emergency baptism (*de necesidad* or *sub conditione*) administered at risk of death. A solemn baptism generally implies the infant survived infancy at least long enough for the ceremony |
| *española* | Spaniard / of Spanish caste | A **casta designation**, not merely nationality. In colonial Mexico's *sistema de castas*, *española* denoted the highest social classification — descent perceived as purely Spanish. This status affected legal rights, marriage options, and which parish register the family would appear in. Genealogically critical |
| *hija legítima* | legitimate daughter | Born in lawful wedlock. The alternative, *hija natural* (natural/illegitimate), would indicate birth outside marriage. Legitimacy affected inheritance and social standing |
| *Don / Doña* | honorific titles | Both parents and both godparents carry *Don/Doña*, marking them as members of the colonial elite or at minimum the respectable gentry class (*gente de razón*). Consistent with the *española* caste designation |
| *padrinos* | godparents (collective) | Covers both *padrino* (godfather, Pedro Gómez) and *madrina* (godmother, Ana López) |
| *parentesco espiritual* | spiritual kinship | The formal doctrine of *compadrazgo* — the spiritual relationship created among godparents, child, and biological parents. Under colonial canon and civil law, this kinship created marriage impediments between these parties and their close relatives. The priest's explicit *advertí* ("I advised them") is a standard legal formula confirming the impediment was declared |

---

### What Matters Genealogically

- **Subject:** Josefa María — casta *española*, legitimate
- **Event:** Solemn baptism on **15 January 1750 (1750-01-15)**
- **Place:** Ciudad de México (Mexico City) — note which parish is on the original document, as Mexico City had multiple parishes serving different populations
- **Father:** Don Juan de Aguilar
- **Mother:** Doña María Ramírez *(note: she retains her maiden surname — standard in Hispanic naming convention; she did not take Aguilar)*
- **Godfather (*padrino*):** Don Pedro Gómez
- **Godmother (*madrina*):** Doña Ana López
- **Officiant:** *infrascrito cura* — unnamed here; check for a rubric/signature on the page

> **Research tip on godparents:** In colonial Mexican practice, godparents (*padrinos*) were frequently relatives or close family friends.
